newsitem.title: CHINA: China economy to grow at more than 10 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China economy to grow at more than 10 pct in 1997.

text.p: China is to see economic growth of more than 10 percent this year, with inflation coming in under six percent, the China Securities newspaper said on Monday.

Successes in macro-economic regulation had helped lay a solid foundation for the stable development of China's economy, the newspaper quoted Qiu Xiaohua, State Statistical Bureau spokesman, as saying.

But the gap between the booming coastal areas and poorer central and western regions was widening and the economy was hampered by inefficiency in the state sector, Qiu said but gave no further details.
China's economy notched up a growth rate of 9.7 percent in 1996 and Beijing has set an official target of eight percent for this year.
Retail price inflation, the benchmark figure China uses to assess national price rises, was kept to 6.1 percent last year down from 14.5 percent in 1995. The official target is six percent for 1997.
